steps.say: In relapsing polychondritis, cartilage is inflamed in flares across ears, nose, airways, and joints. Red tender ears that spare the lobule are the signature. The nose bridge can collapse over time. Flares in cartilage are the definition of the disease.
steps.tx: Cartilage under immune attack in repeating flares is relapsing **polychondritis** (recurrent gristle inflammation): ears, nose, voice box, windpipe branches, and joints take turns swelling, with both auricles eventually hit by **chondritis** (ear gristle inflammation) that always spares the lobule. Red tender ears plus a sore nose indicate polychondritis, since spared lobules never occur in cellulitis.

vis.alt: Inflamed auricle sparing the lobule with nasal bridge collapse in relapsing polychondritis.
vis.caption: Tender violaceous ears with spared lobules mark cartilage flares. Lobule involvement instead indicates infection. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Ear flares are the swelling of the pinna and canal violaceous while the lobule stays normal. The lobule lacks cartilage, which explains the sparing. Bilateral episodes accumulate deformity. Unilateral red ear with spared lobule is still chondritis.
steps.tx: Auricular chondritis gives tender violaceous swelling of **pinna** (outer ear flap) and external canal with **lobule** sparing (soft earlobe untouched), since lobules lack cartilage. Episodes recur bilaterally and accumulate floppy deformity. A tender red pinna with a normal soft lobule indicates chondritis, while lobule involvement indicates cellulitis or erysipelas.

steps.say: Nasal cartilage pain with bleeding and saddle collapse mimics GPA closely. Biopsy separates the two diseases clearly. Bridge collapse is permanent without control. Nasal pain in polychondritis is never dismissed as sinusitis.
steps.tx: Nasal chondritis causes pain, **epistaxis** (nosebleeds), and rhinorrhea with **saddle-nose** deformity (collapsed nasal bridge) from destroyed septal cartilage, indistinguishable from granulomatosis with polyangiitis without biopsy. Septal perforation with crusting indicates either disease. Nasal collapse with ear chondritis indicates polychondritis over GPA.

steps.say: Airway cartilage disease hits up to 50 percent with hoarseness progressing to stridor. Collapse risks fatal obstruction without warning. Flow loops with dynamic CT are the monitors of the threat. New stridor in polychondritis is an emergency.
steps.tx: Laryngotracheal disease affects up to **50 percent**: hoarseness, cough, wheeze, **stridor** (harsh inspiratory noise), and cartilage collapse risking fatal obstruction. **Flow-volume loops** (breathing pattern graphs) with dynamic CT monitor fixed versus variable obstruction. New stridor in known polychondritis indicates emergency airway review, because collapse gives no second warning.

steps.say: Eye inflammation passes 50 percent across episcleritis to scleritis with proptosis. Hearing loss with vertigo is the marker of inner-ear vasculitis strongly. Joints are flared asymmetrically without erosions. All three are scored at every visit.
steps.tx: Ocular disease hits above **50 percent**: episcleritis, **scleritis** (deep scleral inflammation), conjunctivitis, iritis, and retinopathy with **proptosis** (forward eye displacement). Audiovestibular damage brings sensorineural deafness, tinnitus, and vertigo from inner-ear vasculitis. Arthritis stays episodic, asymmetric, non-erosive, and seronegative at costochondral joints. Eyes, ears, and joints are scored at every visit.

steps.say: McAdam criteria need 3 of 6 across ears, joints, nose, eyes, airways, and inner ear together. Bilateral auricular chondritis is the anchor of the count firmly. Biopsy confirms doubtful cases. Three features classify without any waiting.
steps.tx: Counting to three across six territories makes the **McAdam** diagnosis: paired auricular flares, gentle seronegative joint swelling without erosions, nasal gristle pain, eye inflammation, breathing-tube chondritis, and hearing-balance injury. Histologic proof waits for the doubtful few. Three territories classify polychondritis, so counting opens at the first visit.

steps.say: VEXAS strikes men past 50 with UBA1 mutation, macrocytic anaemia, vacuolated marrow, chondritis, Sweet-like rashes, lung shadows, and clots. Mosaicism runs 20 to 60 percent. Fever with cytopenias in an older man requires UBA1 testing.
steps.tx: Fever with low counts in an older man should trigger **VEXAS** testing (vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, autoinflammatory, somatic): a somatic X-linked **UBA1** misprint in men past **50 years** pairing **macrocytic anemia** (oversized red cells) with vacuolated marrow precursors, gristle flares, **Sweet-like** neutrophilic rashes, lung shadows, and venous clots. Mutant myeloid fractions (**mosaicism**) of **20 to 60 percent** in blood confirm clonal disease.

vis.alt: Bone marrow vacuoles with macrocytic anaemia and systemic inflammation in VEXAS syndrome.
vis.caption: Marrow vacuoles with large red cells in a febrile older man mark VEXAS. Mosaicism of 20 to 60 percent confirms it. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Steroids are the controllers of flares while ruxolitinib, azacitidine, or transplant target VEXAS marrow. Low-dose glucocorticoids are the bridge of relapsing disease. Marrow failure is the changer of the plan to transplant. Clone-directed therapy follows sequencing.
steps.tx: Low-dose glucocorticoids with **ruxolitinib** (JAK blockade), **azacitidine** (hypomethylating agent), or allogeneic transplant in selected patients form VEXAS therapy. Relapsing polychondritis flares take steroids with steroid sparers by organ threat. Marrow failure or high-risk clones indicate transplant referral. Sequencing results direct clone therapy, not symptoms alone.
